title: India Just Raised Passport Fees by Up to 67%. The New Rates Hit Tomorrow.
excerpt: A standard 36-page passport now costs ₹2,500, up from ₹1,500. Replacing a lost one under Tatkal will set you back ₹8,500. Here's the full breakdown — and what NRIs applying through missions abroad should know.
body:
The Indian government has revised passport application fees across the board, with the new charges kicking in on July 1, 2026. The changes, notified by the Ministry of External Affairs on June 20 under the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026, replace Schedule IV of the Passports Rules, 1980 — and they apply to every application submitted on or after tomorrow, whether filed in India or through an Indian mission abroad.

## What's Changing

The biggest hit is on replacement passports for lost or damaged documents. A 60-page Tatkal replacement now costs ₹8,500, up from ₹5,500 — a ₹3,000 increase, or roughly 55%. Standard fresh applications have also climbed: a 36-page passport goes from ₹1,500 to ₹2,500 (a 67% jump), and a 60-page one from ₹2,000 to ₹3,500.

Here is the full revised fee structure for adults:

**Fresh or Reissue (Adults)**
- 36-page, Normal: ₹1,500 → ₹2,500 (+₹1,000)
- 36-page, Tatkal: ₹3,500 → ₹5,000 (+₹1,500)
- 60-page, Normal: ₹2,000 → ₹3,500 (+₹1,500)
- 60-page, Tatkal: ₹4,000 → ₹6,000 (+₹2,000)

**Replacement of Lost or Damaged Passport (Adults)**
- 36-page, Normal: ₹3,000 → ₹5,000 (+₹2,000)
- 36-page, Tatkal: ₹5,000 → ₹7,500 (+₹2,500)
- 60-page, Normal: ₹3,500 → ₹6,000 (+₹2,500)
- 60-page, Tatkal: ₹5,500 → ₹8,500 (+₹3,000)

Police Clearance Certificates and Surrender Certificates have also been raised, from ₹500 to ₹750 each.

## Children's Passports

Families with minors under 18 will also see higher costs. A fresh 36-page passport for a child now costs ₹1,750 under normal processing (up from ₹1,000) and ₹4,250 under Tatkal (up from ₹3,000). Replacing a lost child's passport costs ₹4,250 under normal service and ₹6,750 under Tatkal.

There is a small concession: children under eight and senior citizens over 60 continue to receive a 10% discount on standard fresh applications.

## What Hasn't Changed

Passport validity remains untouched. Adult passports are still valid for 10 years, and the existing rules for minors continue to apply. The fee revision covers application charges only — no changes to the document itself or processing timelines.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

For NRIs, the passport is the single most important identity document that ties them to India. Every renewal, every child's first passport, every Police Clearance Certificate for immigration paperwork — all of it flows through the system whose fees just went up.

The revised charges apply uniformly to applications filed through Indian missions abroad, where fees are typically converted to local currency at periodic intervals. NRIs in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, the Gulf states and elsewhere should check with their nearest Indian consulate or embassy for the equivalent dollar, pound or dirham charges, which may be adjusted in the coming weeks to reflect the new INR fee structure.

The timing is particularly significant for NRIs planning summer trips home with family. Those who need passport renewals or fresh passports for children born abroad — a common scenario in the diaspora — will now pay considerably more than they would have just days ago.

## Other July 1 Changes to Watch

The passport fee hike is part of a broader set of regulatory changes taking effect on the same date. The Reserve Bank of India is implementing a new framework to crack down on the mis-selling of financial products like loans and insurance, entitling customers to refunds when forced to purchase unwanted products. The Unique Identification Authority of India is also allowing free Aadhaar email updates through its mobile app until December 31, 2026 — a move that matters for NRIs who need to keep their Aadhaar details current.

And the Income Tax Return filing deadline for the financial year 2025-26 falls on July 31, 2026 — a date that NRIs with Indian income should have on their radar.

The message from the MEA is clear: if you were on the fence about renewing, the window of lower fees has closed.

nri_angle: NRIs renewing passports or applying for children's passports through Indian missions abroad face higher fees starting July 1, with costs rising by up to 67% for standard applications and even more for lost passport replacements.
